title: Selective Classification Under Distribution Shifts
abstract: Studies selective classification under label, covariate, and out-of-distribution shifts and evaluates confidence scores and rejection strategies when test distributions differ from training.

admission.reason: The abstract studies selective classification under several distribution shifts, but the open non-stationary-calibration gap is specifically about continuing sequential adaptation. This is another static train/test-shift study of a capability the existing corpus already covers and does not materially strengthen the remaining gap.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
abstract: Develops selective classifiers for deep networks that can reject predictions to meet a desired risk level with high probability and evaluates performance through the risk-coverage trade-off.

admission.reason: This is an important generic selective-classification foundation, but its abstract contributes the standard deep-network reject/risk-coverage formulation rather than addressing the still-open generation, temporal, or non-stationary gaps. More task-specific selective-prediction candidates in this set provide a better use of a reading slot.

title: On optimum recognition error and reject tradeoff
abstract: Characterizes the trade-off between recognition error and rejection and derives an optimal rejection rule, providing a foundational decision-theoretic basis for selective prediction.

admission.reason: The paper is foundational for recognition-error versus rejection trade-offs, but the capability is subsumed for this review by newer reject-option and risk-coverage treatments that handle the same decision-theoretic role more directly. Identity is also UNCHECKED, so it does not justify a scarce reading slot over the newer candidate.

title: Selective classification under imbalance in multiclass settings: A novel metric for bias-aware risk–coverage evaluation
abstract: Shows that aggregate risk-coverage evaluation can hide class-specific failures under imbalance and proposes class-aware measures and class-conditional rejection analysis.

admission.reason: The abstract shows that aggregate risk-coverage metrics can hide class-specific failures under imbalance, but its proposed evaluation is tied to multiclass imbalance rather than generation, temporal streams, or project-relevant asymmetric decision outcomes. The general lesson about preserving separate denominators is already established in the project context. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: CLIN-SUMM: Incremental Longitudinal Summarization of Clinical Notes Enables Scalable Representation and Early Disease Prediction
abstract: Constructs longitudinal patient representations incrementally, summarizing newly documented information at each encounter while preserving temporal ordering and avoiding future information leakage.

admission.reason: The abstract describes an incremental longitudinal summarization and representation method with temporal ordering and leakage prevention, but it does not show an evaluation method for omission, superseded information, redundancy, or required state updates. Topic wording overlaps gap-5, but the needed evaluation capability is not demonstrated. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Towards Understanding Omission in Dialogue Summarization
abstract: Introduces explicit omission annotations and an omission-detection task for dialogue summaries, evaluating which important source information is absent from generated summaries rather than only measuring overall similarity or faithfulness.

admission.reason: The paper provides explicit omission annotations and omission detection for dialogue summaries, but gap-5 already states that report-level omission has substantial benchmark coverage. The abstract does not add the missing longitudinal dimension of evolving work-item state, due information, supersession, or observation-time correctness.

title: Score-Based Diffusion Priors for Adaptive Conformal Inference under Distribution Shift
abstract: Combines adaptive conformal inference with score-based diffusion priors and online recalibration to improve coverage behavior under temporal and covariate distribution shifts.

admission.reason: The abstract describes adaptive conformal recalibration under temporal and covariate shift, but this capability substantially overlaps the verified online-conformal candidate 2208.08401, which already handles arbitrary distribution shifts. Given the reading-slot constraint and UNCHECKED identity, the verified broader paper is preferred.

title: FACTS&EVIDENCE: An Interactive Tool for Transparent Fine-Grained Factual Verification of Machine-Generated Text
abstract: Provides interactive fine-grained verification by breaking generated text into claims, retrieving multiple evidence sources, and exposing evidence and explanations so users can inspect attribution and support.

admission.reason: The abstract describes an interactive verification tool that decomposes generated text and exposes multiple retrieved evidence sources for human inspection. It does not show a general evaluation method for citation correctness, evidence completeness, partial multi-source support, or joint reliability dimensions, so the tool capability does not materially close the current gaps.

title: RealRoute: Dynamic Query Routing System via Retrieve-then-Verify Paradigm
abstract: Proposes source-agnostic parallel retrieval followed by verification and dynamic routing across heterogeneous information sources, targeting evidence completeness and multi-hop questions rather than relying on one retrieval pass.

admission.reason: This is primarily a retrieval and routing system: parallel source retrieval followed by verification and dynamic routing. Although it targets evidence completeness for multi-hop questions, the abstract does not establish an evaluation method for whether generated compound claims are completely supported. That belongs more naturally to retrieval methodology than Topic 10 evaluation.

title: Investigating Factuality in Long-Form Text Generation: The Roles of Self-Known and Self-Unknown
abstract: Studies factuality at the atomic-claim level in long-form generation and examines whether models can distinguish claims they know from claims they do not know, connecting claim support with uncertainty behavior.

admission.reason: The abstract studies atomic-claim factuality and models' self-known versus self-unknown distinctions, but it does not demonstrate evidence-conditioned support classification or empirical probability calibration against observed correctness. It therefore overlaps atomic-factuality terminology without materially advancing the open completeness or calibration gaps.

title: Unsupervised update summarization of news events
abstract: Presents unsupervised incremental summarization for evolving events, emphasizing novelty, cohesion, and information updates so later summaries avoid simply repeating earlier material.

admission.reason: The paper proposes an incremental news-summarization method emphasizing novelty and reduced repetition, but the abstract does not provide an omission-detection or longitudinal state-evaluation framework. Its useful capability is mainly generation of updates, and the temporal summarization methodology is better represented by the candidate explicitly evaluating comprehensiveness and latency. Identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Atomic Contrastive Verification: Fine-Grained Fact-Checking via Claim Decomposition and Knowledge Graph-Grounded Contrastive Reasoning
abstract: Decomposes text into atomic claims and applies knowledge-graph-grounded contrastive reasoning for fine-grained verification, including contradictions and temporal distortions that sentence-level scoring can obscure.

admission.reason: The abstract combines atomic claim decomposition with knowledge-graph-grounded contradiction and temporal-distortion checking, but it does not address the currently open compound multi-source completeness problem or online calibration problem. Its atomic-verification contribution overlaps stronger verified candidates, and its identity is UNCHECKED.
